task_instruction: Invite elder to an interview about local legends tied to places, offering morning options and a small stipend.
task_details: Email elder named Gordana in selo Zelen Do proposing a morning meeting at the village bench to collect place-based legends that help name sites on the map. State duration about 30–45 minutes, you will bring a printed map and record notes, offer 1,000 RSD, and provide flexibility for other days.
personalized:
Dear Gordana,

Greetings. I am adding local place names and legends to the map of Zelen Do and would love to hear any stories you can share. Could we meet at the village bench on Monday morning for about 30–45 minutes? I will bring a printed map and take brief notes.

I can offer 1,000 RSD for your time. If another day suits you better, please tell me when.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović
(If you want, I can share the stories with the local school.)

Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Request permission to store a drone and Li-po batteries in a specific shelf/box in the office
task_details: Write a short formal-courteous email to the office manager asking permission to keep one quadcopter and two Li-po battery packs in Shelf A inside a lockable box. State basic safety measures, note that you will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and that Li-po batteries will be stored in approved container, provide proof of liability insurance (policy ref), and offer to sign a storage agreement. Include offer to show certificates on request.
personalized:
Dear Ana,

Quick note: I need permission to store my mapping drone (one quadcopter) and two Li-po battery packs in Shelf A of the store room on the second floor. I propose Shelf A, lockable box, labelled for my equipment and accessible only to me. I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container (fireproof battery box, discharge to ~40–60% SOC before storage). I will keep the drone and batteries separated and clearly labelled, and charge batteries only during field trips (not in the office).

I have liability insurance (policy ref: RS-2026-3421) and I can provide a copy of the policy and my UAV training certificate (UAV/drone mapping course) if you want. I’m happy to sign a simple storage agreement or add a clause to our office rules.

If you prefer a different location or additional precautions (ventilation, signage), let me know and I’ll adjust. Thank you for considering this.

Best regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer
(43.8563 N, 18.4131 E)

task_details: Ask the landlord/manager to allow installation of a small lockable metal cabinet in the ground-floor storeroom. personalized:
Hello Mark,

I’m writing to propose installing a small lockable metal cabinet in the ground-floor storeroom for my drone and batteries. I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container placed on a fireproof tray inside the cabinet. The cabinet would be labelled, locked, and used exclusively by me. Charging will not take place inside the building; batteries will be charged only during fieldwork using a portable charger and under supervision.

I follow applicable national UAV regulations and have liability insurance (policy ref: RS-INS-7789). I’m prepared to cover the minor cost of the cabinet and installation and to sign a simple written agreement. Please let me know if you approve or if you prefer extra measures (sensor, signage, or dedicated room).

Regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst

task_instruction: Ask for temporary storage during winter months with temperature control
task_details: Request temporary permission to store the drone and batteries in an interior office (not near windows) during winter months. personalized:
Dear Jelena,

Quick note about equipment storage for the winter season. I need to keep my drone and three Li-po packs in the office from November through March while I’m running village mapping projects. I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container, and I prefer an interior office (away from direct sunlight) to keep temperatures between roughly 15–25°C. If the office cannot guarantee that range I will bring batteries home during the hot months.

I have liability insurance (policy ref: GIS-2026-556) and can sign a short agreement covering storage terms. If you want, I can bring the approved battery container and place a small label and emergency contact inside.

Thanks for considering this.

Best,
Marko

Hello Ivana,

If you’re comfortable allowing me to store my drone and batteries on site, I’d like to offer a short 20-minute briefing for staff about battery and drone safety. The briefing will cover how I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and that Li-po batteries stored in approved container, basic do’s and don’ts around the storage area, and what to do in an emergency. I’ll bring the approved storage container and label everything.

I carry liability insurance (policy ref: RS-GIS-9102) and will sign any acknowledgement form you require. Training is free and I’ll keep it practical and short.

Let me know if you want to set a time.

Regards,
Marko

Dear Zoran,

I’m requesting permission to store four Li-po battery packs in the equipment room. I will segregate batteries by state-of-charge into two approved containers labelled 'Storage, 40–60% SOC' and 'To Use'. Regards,
Marko

task_instruction: Ask permission to store batteries and offer to sign a waiver releasing landlord from certain liabilities

personalized:
Hello Branka,

I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container, but I understand the landlord may want additional protection. I’m willing to sign a reasonable waiver releasing the landlord from liabilities specifically related to my equipment and storage. My liability insurance reference is RS-WAV-7088 and I can provide a copy.

If you prefer, you can send the waiver wording to me or have your counsel draft it and I will review. I want to make sure we both feel comfortable with the arrangement.

Best,
Marko

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: Email to a landlord or office manager about storing a drone and batteries in the workspace.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Direct and practical with a formal-courteous tone: state safety precautions and legal/regulatory notes briefly, and propose storage arrangements in clear sentences. Provide assurance about insurance and offer to sign an agreement.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Use safety and compliance phrases: "follow manufacturer storage guidelines", "Li-po batteries stored in approved container". Include concise proposals: "I propose shelf A, lockable box, labelled" and closing assurances: "I have liability insurance (policy ref...)."

task_instruction: Request permission and offer to rotate battery stock to minimize age-related risk
task_details: Ask to store multiple batteries but commit to rotating stock so no battery remains stored for more than three months, adhere to manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container, provide insurance ref and offer to log dates and replace old batteries promptly.
personalized:
Dear Ognjen,

I request permission to store several Li-po battery packs for operational needs with the condition that I will rotate stock so no battery sits in storage for longer than three months. I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container and maintain a simple log with dates of storage.

My liability insurance reference is RS-ROT-1552. I will remove or replace older batteries promptly and share the log with you on request.

Regards,
Marko

persona.name: Marko Petrović
persona.demographics: Belgrade, Serbia; Serbian; raised in a small village near Niš, has lived and worked across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Croatia
persona.profession: Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer — Village-scale mapping and spatial data analyst
persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

Best regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst

Marko

task_instruction: Provide troubleshooting steps for reprojecting a raster between EPSG codes.
task_details: Recipients need compact steps to reproject a large orthophoto from EPSG:32634 to EPSG:3857 using GDAL and QGIS, with an example gdalwarp command and a note about resampling choice.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open orthophoto.qgz > Layers > Right-click raster > Export > Save as... and set Target CRS to EPSG:3857. For command-line, example: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:3857 -r cubic input_ortho_EPSG32634.tif output_ortho_EPSG3857.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping; use -r bilinear or -r cubic for continuous imagery (avoid nearest for photos). Watch output file size and add -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co TILED=YES to reduce size. If you want, I can review your project file. Ping me if you hit slow reprojection or weird georeferencing.

task_instruction: Explain how to clip a large raster to a village boundary in QGIS and GDAL.
task_details: Show inline steps to clip a 10 GB orthophoto using a polygon boundary (village_boundary.shp). Include a gdalwarp example with -cutline and advice on memory and tiling.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open sample.qgz > Layers > Right-click orthophoto > Export > Clip to Layer (select village_boundary). CLI example: gdalwarp -cutline village_boundary.shp -crop_to_cutline -dstalpha large_ortho.tif village_clip.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping (ensure both have same EPSG). For very large files, add -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=LZW and process by tiles (gdal_translate + gdal_merge). If you want, I can review your project file. Tell me file sizes and I’ll suggest a tile/VM workflow.

task_instruction: Give steps to generate a 1 m DEM from a point cloud and create contours.
task_details: Participants have a classified point cloud (LAZ) and need to produce a 1 m raster DEM and 1 m contours. Include PDAL/gdal commands and QGIS steps; mention CRS and output filenames.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:

In QGIS, open dem_1m.tif > Raster > Extraction > Contour (Interval=1) > save as contours_1m.shp. Tip: check projection before clipping and ensure ground-classified points only for DEM. If you want, I can review your project file. Share the LAZ or dem and I’ll verify classification and contour quality.

task_instruction: Explain how to compute hillshade and slope layers for map visualization.
task_details: Short instructions to generate hillshade and slope from DEM in QGIS and gdal, include example commands, recommended z-factor, and styling tips for print maps.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:

For print, use hillshade as a multiply blend under your coloured DEM or contours to keep readability. If you want, I can review your project file. I can suggest layer order and opacity for A3 print maps.

task_instruction: Share instructions for mosaicking multiple drone orthos into a seamless mosaic.
task_details: Team members need to merge five overlapping ortho tiles into one seamless file; include gdalwarp/gdal_merge examples and advice on edges, feathering, and compression.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Use gdalwarp to mosaic and match resolution: gdalwarp -dstalpha -r cubic -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=JPEG ortho_01.tif ortho_02.tif ortho_03.tif ortho_04.tif ortho_05.tif mosaic_ortho.tif. Alternatively gdal_merge -o mosaic_ortho.tif -of GTiff -co COMPRESS=JPEG *.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping; use -overwrite and add -wo NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS for speed. Feather seamlines in your photogrammetry package or use linear blending if you see contrast jumps. If you want, I can review your project file. Share a small subset and I’ll test blending parameters.

task_instruction: Give concise steps to prepare and push edits to OpenStreetMap.
task_details: Participants used JOSM and iD in the workshop; provide steps for preparing data (convert to .osm or .gpx), conflict checks, tagging conventions for rural features, and a reminder on imagery offsets and source tags.

Thanks again — quick follow-up:

Tagging tips: highway=track for unpaved, surface=gravel, building=yes with building:levels if known. Tip: check projection before clipping and always add source=survey or source=drone_ortho_2025. If you want, I can review your project file. I can also preview your changeset and suggest edits to avoid conflicts.

task_instruction: Explain how to clean GPX tracks from noisy GPS trajectories and convert to shapefile.
task_details: Provide steps to filter noise, remove low-accuracy points, simplify track, and export to ESRI Shapefile. Include QGIS processing steps and ogr2ogr example; mention filtering by PDOP/hdop attribute.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open tracks.gpx in QGIS > convert GPX track points to layer > Filter out points with hdop > 5 or invalid timestamps (use attribute table or SQL). Use Simplify Geometries (Tolerance 2 m) to reduce jitter then Merge lines. Export as Shapefile: Right-click > Export > Save Features As > ESRI Shapefile. CLI example: ogr2ogr -f "ESRI Shapefile" clean_tracks.shp tracks.gpx -where "hdop < 5". Tip: check projection before clipping and reproject to local UTM for distance-based simplification. If you want, I can review your project file. Share a sample GPX and I’ll clean and return a simplified track.

task_instruction: Provide a short how-to for joining CSV attribute data to a spatial layer.
task_details: Participants have a parcels.shp and a CSV with parcel_id and owner info. Show how to join on parcel_id in QGIS and note common pitfalls (string vs integer). Include Field Calculator example.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:

After join, export layer to new Shapefile to make join permanent: Right-click > Export > Save Features As. Tip: check projection before clipping and ensure no extra spaces or BOM in CSV header. If you want, I can review your project file. Send the CSV and shapefile and I’ll verify join matches and clean attributes.

task_instruction: Write concise guidance on simplifying a road network for fast web rendering.

task_instruction: Provide steps to create MBTiles/XYZ tiles for a village web map.
task_details: Include gdal2tiles and tip on zoom levels and overview size. Provide an example command to produce MBTiles and advise on hosting options (GitHub Pages/tileserver-gl).
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Use gdal2tiles or gdal_translate + gdaladdo for MBTiles. Example: gdal2tiles.py -z 12-18 -r bilinear mosaic_ortho.tif tiles_folder. Tip: check projection before clipping and reproject to WebMercator EPSG:3857 when creating XYZ tiles. Host via simple static server, tileserver-gl, or GitHub Pages for raster tiles. If you want, I can review your project file. Tell me desired zooms and I’ll suggest tile settings.

task_instruction: Describe an automated QGIS ModelBuilder workflow to batch clip rasters.
task_details: Participants want a reusable model: input raster folder, polygon boundary, output folder. Provide model outline and an example expression, and mention logging.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open QGIS > Processing > Graphical Modeler > add inputs: Raster folder (multiple), Vector layer (boundary). Add algorithm: Clip raster by mask layer > set output file path as expression: concat('output_folder/', basename(@raster), '_clip.tif'). Run model on batch. Tip: check projection before clipping and ensure all rasters share CRS or add reprojection step in model (gdalwarp). Save model as clip_by_village.model and share with volunteers. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll help add logging and error handling to the model.

Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Quick Python snippet (rasterio):
with rasterio.open('input.tif') as src:
    out_meta = src.meta.copy()
    out_meta.update({'crs': 'EPSG:3857'})
    reprojected = 'input_3857.tif'
    # use rasterio.warp.reproject then rasterio.mask.mask with village_boundary.geojson
Tip: check projection before clipping and run in a conda env with rasterio installed (conda create -n geo rasterio fiona). For GDAL CLI alternative: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:3857 input.tif output_3857.tif && gdalwarp -cutline village_boundary.shp -crop_to_cutline output_3857.tif clipped.tif. If you want, I can review your project file. Send the script and I’ll adapt it to your folder structure.

task_instruction: Provide a short backup and version control workflow for GIS projects.
task_details: Recommend simple rules using Git for project files, Git LFS or Nextcloud for large rasters, naming conventions and periodic backups. Include example Git commands.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Keep QGIS project (.qgz) and scripts in Git repo; store large rasters and ortho in Nextcloud or with Git LFS. Example git steps: git init; git add project.qgz scripts/; git commit -m "initial project". For large files use: git lfs track "*.tif" then git add .gitattributes. Tip: check projection before clipping and include dataset version in filename (v1, v2). Schedule weekly sync: rsync to external drive and push to Nextcloud. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll help set up a repo or Nextcloud folder and .gitignore.

task_instruction: Send field survey tips for collecting GPS points with a handheld receiver.
task_details: Provide concise practical tips to volunteers: receiver settings, sample interval, averaging, taking photos with coordinates, and post-processing advice. Include coordinates example and mention GPX export.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
In the field use handheld GPS in WAAS/RTK if available, set logging interval to 1–5 s, take at least 3 averaged readings per POI spaced 10–30 s apart, and take a photo with phone for context (embed coordinates later). Export tracks as GPX and name files like survey_2025-06-15.gpx. Tip: check projection before clipping after import and convert GPX to local UTM for distance calculations (EPSG:32634). If you want, I can review your project file. Send a sample GPX and I’ll check completeness and accuracy.

task_instruction: Summarize UAV safety and legal checklist for planning village flights.
task_details: Include pre-flight checks, permissions, NOTAM, proximity to people/animals, max altitude recommendations, and data privacy reminders for villagers.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Before flight check: drone serviceability, batteries, propellers, and firmware. Confirm permissions with municipality and check NOTAMs (local aviation authority). Tip: check projection before clipping and record GCP coordinates in WGS84 (lat/lon) and local UTM. Respect privacy: avoid collecting identifiable faces or private courtyards without consent. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll also help draft a short consent note for locals.

task_instruction: Explain how to extract contour lines from a DEM and label them for printing.
task_details: Provide concise steps: use gdaldem or QGIS contour tool, label contours every 5 m, convert labels to annotations or use rule-based labeling for major contours. Include example commands.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Use QGIS > Raster > Extraction > Contour (Interval = 5) to get contours_5m.shp. CLI alternative: gdaldem contour dem_1m.tif contours_5m.shp -i 5. For labeling, use Rule-based labeling: major contours (every 25 m) thicker and labeled; minor contours lighter. Tip: check projection before clipping and reproject contours to local UTM for proper distance units. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check label placement and suggest offsets for legibility.

task_instruction: Provide a short QA checklist before delivering datasets to the municipality.
task_details: Include checks: CRS, metadata, attribute completeness, topology, small geometry fixes, file naming, and delivery package contents. Be concise and actionable.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Quick QA before delivery: verify CRS is correct (EPSG noted), include README/metadata, check attribute completeness (no NULLs in key fields), run topology (no dangles for closed features), simplify small slivers (remove <1 m2 polygons), validate geometries, and standardize filenames (no spaces; include date and version). Tip: check projection before clipping and include sample coordinates in metadata. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll run these checks and return a short QA report.

task_instruction: Outline how to build a rule-based symbology for building ages and materials.
task_details: Explain creating classification rules in QGIS based on an 'age' and 'material' attribute, provide sample expressions and styling guidance for map legibility.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open buildings.shp > Symbology > Rule-based > add rules like "age < 1950" -> brown fill for 'historic', "age >=1950 AND material='concrete'" -> grey fill for 'modern concrete'. Use expressions: "age" < 1950 and "material" = 'stone'. Tip: check projection before clipping (labels and buffer sizes depend on units). Keep colour palette limited and add a small legend entry for each rule. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll suggest final colours and label rules for readability.

task_instruction: Give compact instructions to use Sentinel-2 data for vegetation change detection.
task_details: Show steps to download Sentinel-2, compute NDVI for two dates, subtract rasters to find change, and mask small disturbances. Include Copernicus link and example band expressions.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Download Sentinel-2 L2A from Copernicus (https://scihub.copernicus.eu) for two dates > load band 8 (NIR) and band 4 (red). Compute NDVI for each: (B8 - B4)/(B8 + B4) and save ndvi_2019.tif, ndvi_2024.tif. Use Raster Calculator: ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 > save as ndvi_change.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping and align/resample rasters to same grid (use gdalwarp -tr 10 10). Mask small changes <0.05 to remove noise. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check cloud cover and recommend dates to use.

task_instruction: Prepare brief guidance on packaging a QGIS project for volunteers (data and project file).
task_details: Participants need directions to collect relative paths, package small rasters, include README, and export project as a portable package or GeoPackage. Include step to check 'relative paths' and example filenames.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
In QGIS Project Properties > General > set Save paths = Relative. Collect small rasters and vector layers into folder "village_package_2025" and update project to point to those files. Option: Export as GeoPackage (Open sample.qgz > Layers > Right-click > Export > Save as GeoPackage) to include vectors; embed rasters separately or use virtual rasters (.vrt). Tip: check projection before clipping and ensure all files are present before zipping. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll create a packaged folder and test it on a clean machine.

task_instruction: Send a short troubleshooting note for mismatched layer alignment after import.
task_details: Explain quick checks when layers don't line up: CRS mismatch, datum shift, units, broken geotransform. Give commands to inspect CRS and an ogrinfo/gdalinfo example.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
If layers don’t align, first check CRS: Layer Properties > Source > Coordinate Reference System. CLI: gdalinfo raster.tif and ogrinfo -al vector.shp. Common fixes: reproject layer (Raster: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:32634) or vector (ogr2ogr -t_srs EPSG:32634 out.shp in.shp). Tip: check projection before clipping and confirm datum (WGS84 vs local). If still off by a fixed offset, check for missing affine transform or wrong units. If you want, I can review your project file. Send screenshots and file names and I’ll diagnose the offset.

task_instruction: Provide short guidance on sharing large raster subsets with volunteers via Nextcloud/WeTransfer.
task_details: Advise on creating smaller tiles or compressed subsets, recommended compression options, and suggested folder structure and filenames for uploads.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Create smaller subsets: gdal_translate -projwin xmin ymin xmax ymax input.tif subset.tif and compress: gdal_translate -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co JPEG_QUALITY=85 input.tif out_compressed.tif. Zip or tar.gz folder and upload to Nextcloud or use WeTransfer for >2 GB. Tip: check projection before clipping and include a small preview PNG for quick inspection. Suggested folder structure: data/ortho/, data/dem/, project/sample.qgz, README.md. If you want, I can review your project file. Tell me which files to package and I’ll prepare an upload-ready archive.

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

task_instruction: Propose metadata and standards compliance clauses (ISO and INSPIRE).

personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This message proposes metadata and standards compliance language for the planning dataset. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: planning_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) accompanied by ISO 19115 metadata and a descriptive metadata record including lineage, scale, and accuracy fields. We recommend an INSPIRE-like metadata profile for interoperability. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Provider shall deliver metadata compliant with ISO 19115 and the agreed metadata profile in Exhibit F at the time of data delivery." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can supply a metadata template populated with sample fields if that helps. Sincerely, Marko Petrović

Please review the proposed payment terms for the multi-village mapping contract. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Proposed payment schedule: 30% on contract signature, 40% on interim delivery (first five villages), 30% on final acceptance after QA. personalized:

personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please review the proposed language regarding third-party basemaps used in production. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0 for the municipal data only. Data deliverable: project_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and final PDF maps. Third-party basemaps (commercial or open-source) are excluded from the CC license; Recipient is responsible for obtaining basemap licenses if needed. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Provider disclaims any rights to third-party basemaps used in the composite products; Recipient assumes responsibility for third-party license compliance." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can list the third-party sources used during production for your review. Best, Marko Petrović

persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: Email to a supplier requesting calibration services for surveying equipment and asking for turnaround and cost.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Businesslike and succinct with clear itemization of equipment (in-line) and expected service level. Use short sentences to list models and calibration specs, ask for ETA and pricing, and end with a polite call to action.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Include model-specific phrasing: "Total station (Model X), GPS receiver (Model Y)" and service details: "calibration to manufacturer's spec, certificate provided". Use direct requests: "Please provide cost estimate and lead time", and closers: "Awaiting your quote."

task_instruction: Ask for calibration and verification of accuracy after a software update.
task_details: Request calibration to manufacturer's spec and post-update verification for Total station (Sokkia Set630RK, S/N SET630-007) after we apply a major firmware update. Ask supplier to verify instrument accuracy after update, provide certificate, cost and lead time. Mention we will ship after confirmation.
personalized: FYI: We plan to apply a major firmware update to Total station (Sokkia Set630RK, S/N SET630-007). Please provide calibration to manufacturer's spec and a post-update accuracy verification. Provide certificate, cost and lead time. I will ship after your confirmation of requirements. Please provide cost estimate and lead time. Awaiting your quote. Regards, Marko
